items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: The one you're referring to I think is the one that was with Fletcher Henderson.

ctx.x: Well I know Buster quite well.

Now there is two Buster Bailey's. The one you're referring to I think is the one that was with Fletcher Henderson. Yeah. Well there is another one that was from Dallas that went to Europe and never came back. Well I don't know. Did he play Clarence also? Yes he was terrific. Really?
I didn't know that. Two of them.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: And Geechee Robinson, you once told me about, you were with Fletcher Henderson for a while.

ctx.x: Mostly with me. Mostly with you.
And Geechee Robinson, you once told me about, you were with Fletcher Henderson for a while.
After he left my band. Yeah.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: After he left my band, he went a little while with Fletcher when Fletcher was on the road.

ctx.x: I don't know, Dick, but I assume that he is. After he left my band, he went a little while with Fletcher when Fletcher was on the road. He was always a fickle fellow, wanting a gold, gold, gold, so I imagine he just kept running. And I never heard from him, he's one of the characters that never did Carl Strawn much.
Yeah. But what did he do when the moon changed? Can you tell me?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: like all the numbers that Prince and McCormick Hawkins were playing Stampede and the numbers that Henderson had.

ctx.x: Well what about Herschel Evans then? Was he a good reader when he came?

No, Herschel couldn't read music. How I met Herschel Evans, I was getting ready to leave here and they used to have the Dixie Series and there was a band that Herschel came here with, with a team from Wichita Falls that year. The name of this band was the TNT band and Jimmy Westbrook was the drummer, he's a left-handed drummer. He's now living in Los Angeles and Herschel was playing alto and playing a date up at the old Pelican ball and I met Herschel then and we all left on the same train. I was going to Dallas…
